text: Sardar Patel Institute of Technology (SPIT) was established in 1995 as an autonomous engineering college located at Bhavan's Campus, Munshi Nagar, Andheri (West), Mumbai 400058, Maharashtra, India. It is managed by the Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan trust. SPIT is permanently affiliated with the University of Mumbai and approved by the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE), New Delhi.
title: About Sardar Patel Institute of Technology

text: In 2017, SPIT was granted academic autonomy by the University Grants Commission (UGC) and the University of Mumbai. This autonomy allows the institute to design an industry-relevant curriculum, implement innovative teaching methodologies, and conduct independent examinations and continuous assessments.
title: About Sardar Patel Institute of Technology

text: Spread over 47 acres in the lush green Munshi Nagar campus of Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan, SPIT shares the premises with Sardar Patel College of Engineering (SPCE) and S.P. Jain Institute of Management and Research (SPJIMR). The campus houses modern instructional buildings, research incubation centers, student amenities, and sports facilities.
title: About Sardar Patel Institute of Technology

text: To build a renowned institute providing high-quality engineering education and research with ethical values, fostering innovation, entrepreneurship, and societal impact.
title: Vision, Mission and Quality Policy

text: M1: Deliver student-centric learning experiences through rigorous academic frameworks and state-of-the-art laboratories. M2: Promote interdisciplinary research, industrial collaborations, and continuous innovation. M3: Nurture leaders and entrepreneurs equipped with critical thinking, problem-solving skills, and deep ethical commitment to community development.
title: Vision, Mission and Quality Policy

text: SPIT is dedicated to achieving excellence in technical education through continual improvement of pedagogical methods, state-of-the-art infrastructure, human resources development, and active engagement with industry stakeholders.
title: Vision, Mission and Quality Policy

text: Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan was founded in 1938 by Dr. K. M. Munshi with the blessings of Mahatma Gandhi. Sardar Patel College of Engineering (SPCE) was established in 1962 as a government-aided institute. In 1995, Bhavan's trust established SPIT as an unaided engineering wing offering Electronics Engineering, Computer Engineering, and Information Technology.
title: History of Sardar Patel Institute of Technology

text: In 2005, SPIT became an independent entity separated from SPCE. Postgraduate Master of Computer Applications (MCA) was introduced in 2008, followed by M.Tech degrees in Computer Engineering and Electronics & Telecommunication. In 2021, SPIT introduced new undergraduate courses in Computer Science and Engineering (Data Science) and Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning.
title: History of Sardar Patel Institute of Technology

text: The Governing Body is headed by prominent industrialists, educators, and representatives from Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan, AICTE, Directorate of Technical Education (DTE), and Mumbai University. It provides strategic direction, oversees fiscal health, and approves key academic and infrastructural expansions.
title: Governance, Leadership and Administration

text: The Academic Council is the apex academic decision-making body of the autonomous institute. It approves curricula formulated by the Boards of Studies (BoS) for each department, ratifies examination results, introduces new specializations, and ensures compliance with UGC and AICTE guidelines.
title: Governance, Leadership and Administration

text: The SPIT Central Library holds more than 28,000 volumes of technical books, subscriptions to IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, ScienceDirect, SpringerLink, and national and international journals. The library is fully automated with KOHA LMS and provides RFID-enabled book checkouts and 24/7 digital access.
title: Campus Facilities and Infrastructure

text: The institute houses over 35 dedicated laboratories equipped with modern hardware, high-performance computing clusters with NVIDIA GPU workstations, 1 Gbps high-speed campus-wide fiber internet, cloud sandbox environments, and specialized IoT and robotics research setups.
title: Campus Facilities and Infrastructure

text: Separate on-campus hostel facilities are provided for male and female students with dining mess, recreation rooms, and Wi-Fi connectivity. The campus also features open sports grounds for cricket and football, basketball courts, an auditorium, and subsidized food cafeterias.
title: Campus Facilities and Infrastructure

text: The Department of Computer Engineering at SPIT was established in 1995 and offers B.Tech. in Computer Engineering (intake of 120 students), M.Tech. in Computer Engineering, and Ph.D. in Computer Engineering. The department is accredited by NBA (National Board of Accreditation) under Tier-I format.
title: Department of Computer Engineering

text: The department features specialized laboratories including: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Lab, High-Performance Computing Lab, Cloud Computing & Big Data Lab, Cybersecurity and Network Forensics Lab, Software Engineering Lab, and Computer Vision & Robotics Lab.
title: Department of Computer Engineering

text: Key subject tracks encompass Generative AI (CE413), Natural Language Processing, Deep Learning, Distributed Systems, Compiler Design, Database Management Systems, Blockchain Technology, and Human-Computer Interaction.
title: Department of Computer Engineering

text: The Department of Information Technology offers an undergraduate B.Tech. in Information Technology with an annual intake of 60 students. It prepares engineers in web and enterprise software systems, information security, data engineering, and ubiquitous cloud architectures.
title: Department of Information Technology

text: Laboratories include: Enterprise Software Systems Lab, Mobile Computing Lab, Information Security and Cryptography Lab, and Data Analytics Lab. Faculty and students regularly publish papers in IEEE, Springer, and ACM conferences.
title: Department of Information Technology

text: Established in 1995, the Department of Electronics and Telecommunication Engineering (EXTC) offers B.Tech. in EXTC (intake 120), M.Tech. in EXTC, and Ph.D. The department is NBA Tier-I accredited and emphasizes embedded systems, signal processing, and 5G wireless networks.
title: Department of Electronics and Telecommunication Engineering

text: Equipped with Keysight RF Vector Signal Analyzers, Cadence VLSI EDA tools, Texas Instruments DSP and IoT kits, and MATLAB campus-wide licenses. Research tracks include IoT Architectures, VLSI Chip Design, Optical Communication, and Embedded AI.
title: Department of Electronics and Telecommunication Engineering

text: To meet the burgeoning demand for data-centric and machine intelligence engineering, SPIT launched the B.Tech. in CSE (Data Science) with an intake of 60 students and B.Tech. in CSE (AI & Machine Learning). The curriculum blends statistical foundations, deep neural architectures, MLOps, and big data pipelines.
title: Department of Computer Science and Engineering (Data Science)

text: GPU computing servers with CUDA support, industry mentorship from leading data science enterprises, and hands-on capstone projects spanning healthcare AI, financial analytics, and autonomous systems.
title: Department of Computer Science and Engineering (Data Science)

text: The MCA programme at SPIT is a two-year postgraduate degree designed to prepare IT professionals and system architects. The approved intake is 60 students per batch, admitted via MAH-MCA-CET.
title: Department of Master of Computer Applications (MCA)

text: Focuses on Full-Stack Development, Cloud Computing, DevOps, Software Quality Assurance, and Business Analytics. MCA students have mandatory 6-month industry internships in the final semester.
title: Department of Master of Computer Applications (MCA)

text: The department lays the mathematical and scientific foundation for all first-year engineering students. Courses include Engineering Mathematics I & II, Engineering Physics, Engineering Chemistry, Professional Communication, and Environmental Studies.
title: Department of Applied Sciences and Humanities

text: Hosts the central Product Realization and Makerspace lab equipped with 3D printers, laser cutters, CNC milling machines, and PCB fabrication units, introducing freshman students to design thinking and rapid prototyping.
title: Department of Applied Sciences and Humanities

section: Eligibility Criteria for First Year B.Tech
text: Candidate must be an Indian National and must have passed HSC (Std. XII) examination of Maharashtra State Board of Secondary and Higher Secondary Education or equivalent with Physics and Mathematics as compulsory subjects along with one of Chemistry/Biotechnology/Biology/Technical Vocational subjects. Candidate must have obtained at least 45% marks (at least 40% marks for Backward Class categories, EWS and Persons with Disabilities from Maharashtra State).
title: Undergraduate Admissions and Eligibility Criteria

text: Admission for Maharashtra State Candidates is based on non-zero score in MHT-CET conducted by the State Common Entrance Test Cell. Admission for All India Candidates is based on percentile score in JEE (Main) Paper I over MHT-CET score.
title: Undergraduate Admissions and Eligibility Criteria

text: 80% of seats are filled through the Centralized Admission Process (CAP) rounds conducted by the State CET Cell, Maharashtra. 20% of seats are Institute Level Quota seats filled strictly according to merit following guidelines issued by the Directorate of Technical Education (DTE).
title: Undergraduate Admissions and Eligibility Criteria

text: The fee structure for First Year B.Tech at SPIT as approved by the Fee Regulating Authority (FRA), Maharashtra for Academic Year 2026-27 is approximately: Tuition Fee: Rs. 1,52,174; Development Fee: Rs. 22,826; Total Interim Fee: Rs. 1,75,000 per annum. University and eligibility fees are payable separately as per Mumbai University circulars.
title: Fee Structure and Payment Guidelines

text: SC / ST / VJNT / SBC students receive 100% Tuition Fee waiver under Government of Maharashtra social welfare schemes. OBC and EBC (Economically Backward Class) students are eligible for 50% Tuition Fee concession. TFWS (Tuition Fee Waiver Scheme) candidates pay only the Development Fee and exam charges.
title: Fee Structure and Payment Guidelines

text: Eligible students can avail MahaDBT scholarships including Rajarshi Chhatrapati Shahu Maharaj Shikshan Shulkh Shishyavrutti Yojna (EBC), Dr. Panjabrao Deshmukh Vasatigruh Nirvah Bhatta Yojna for hostel maintenance, and post-matric scholarships for SC, ST, OBC, and Minority communities.
title: Financial Aid and Scholarships

text: SPIT Alumni Association and Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan provide merit-cum-means financial assistance for needy students with exemplary academic records, ensuring that no meritorious candidate drops out due to financial constraints.
title: Financial Aid and Scholarships

text: SPIT maintains an exceptional placement track record with consistently over 95% placement rate for eligible students. For the graduating class, the Highest International Package offered stood at Rs. 1.1 Crore per annum, the Highest Domestic Package was Rs. 54.5 Lakhs per annum, and the Average Overall CTC across all engineering branches was Rs. 15.2 Lakhs per annum.
title: Training & Placement Cell and Placement Statistics

text: Over 120 marquee companies recruit from SPIT every year. Top recruiters include Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs, JP Morgan Chase, Barclays, Deutsche Bank, Oracle, Cisco, Adobe, Samsung R&D, Qualcomm, and Nvidia.
title: Training & Placement Cell and Placement Statistics

text: The Training and Placement Cell facilitates pre-final year summer internships with average stipends ranging from Rs. 40,000 to Rs. 1,50,000 per month. A high percentage of interns receive Pre-Placement Offers (PPOs) before their final year starts.
title: Training & Placement Cell and Placement Statistics

text: SPIT has signed active MOUs with companies including Tata Consultancy Services, L&T Infotech, Texas Instruments, Intel Technology India, and AWS Academy. These partnerships sponsor research labs, deliver expert guest lectures, and conduct industrial hackathons.
title: Industry MOUs and Corporate Collaborations

text: Through collaborations with investment banking firms like Morgan Stanley and Nomura, SPIT runs specialized technical workshops on algorithmic trading, quantitative finance, and low-latency distributed microservices.
title: Industry MOUs and Corporate Collaborations

text: Active student chapters include IEEE SPIT Student Branch, Computer Society of India (CSI) SPIT Chapter, ACM Student Chapter, and IETE Student Forum. These bodies organize technical seminars, coding contests, and paper presentation conferences.
title: Student Activities, Technical Committees and Student Bodies

text: Rotaract Club of SPIT spearheads community outreach, blood donation drives, and environmental sustainability campaigns. Mudra is the cultural society encompassing music, drama, fine arts, and literary events.
title: Student Activities, Technical Committees and Student Bodies

text: Oculus is the flagship annual national-level techno-cultural festival of SPIT attracting over 8,000 students across the country. It features high-stakes hackathons, robotics challenges, coding marathons, gaming leagues, alongside musical performances, dance battles, and fashion showcases.
title: Annual Festivals: Oculus and Spoorthi

text: Spoorthi is the inter-collegiate and intra-collegiate sports tournament celebrating athletic prowess in cricket, football, basketball, badminton, table tennis, athletics, and chess.
title: Annual Festivals: Oculus and Spoorthi

text: Sardar Patel Technology Business Incubator (SP-TBI) is an initiative supported by the Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India. It provides budding student and faculty startups with co-working space, seed funding, intellectual property guidance, legal advisory, and high-profile investor pitching opportunities.
title: Sardar Patel Technology Business Incubator (SP-TBI)

text: The student-run E-Cell organizes E-Summit, startup expos, business plan competitions, and founder talk shows, cultivating a venture creation mindset among the student body.
title: Sardar Patel Technology Business Incubator (SP-TBI)

text: Under autonomy, SPIT operates on a Choice Based Credit System (CBCS) complying with the National Education Policy (NEP 2020) and AICTE model guidelines. A typical B.Tech. degree requires completion of approximately 160 credits distributed over eight semesters.
title: Academic Curriculum Structure and Credit System

text: Students with CGPA >= 7.5 and no active backlog can opt for an additional Honors degree (e.g. B.Tech CE with Honors in AI) or a Minor degree (e.g. Minor in Finance or Minor in IoT) by earning an extra 18-20 credits through prescribed elective tracks and approved MOOCs like NPTEL/Swayam.
title: Academic Curriculum Structure and Credit System

text: Evaluation for each theory course comprises: In-Semester Evaluation (ISE) carrying 20% weightage (quizzes, micro-projects, assignments); Mid-Semester Examination (MSE) carrying 30% weightage (conducted at mid-term for 1.5 hours); and End-Semester Examination (ESE) carrying 50% weightage (comprehensive 3-hour examination covering the entire syllabus).
title: Examination Scheme and Evaluation Model

text: SPIT uses a 10-point absolute grading scale: O (Outstanding, 10 grade points, >=85 marks), A+ (Excellent, 9 points, 75-84), A (Very Good, 8 points, 70-74), B+ (Good, 7 points, 60-69), B (Above Average, 6 points, 55-59), C (Average, 5 points, 50-54), P (Pass, 4 points, 40-49), and F (Fail, 0 points, <40 marks). Semester Grade Performance Average (SGPA) and Cumulative Grade Performance Average (CGPA) are computed accordingly.
title: Examination Scheme and Evaluation Model

text: A student must maintain a minimum attendance of 75% in aggregate across all registered courses in each semester to be eligible to appear for the End-Semester Examination. Condonation up to 10% (i.e. relaxation down to 65%) may be granted by the Principal exclusively on genuine medical grounds accompanied by registered hospital certificates.
title: Academic Regulations, Attendance Policy and ATKT Rules

text: A student is permitted to keep term (progress to the next academic year) only if the total number of failing credit backlogs at the end of the preceding year does not exceed the threshold set by the Academic Council (maximum of 4 failed heads of passing in preceding semesters).
title: Academic Regulations, Attendance Policy and ATKT Rules

text: CE413 - Generative AI is a Program Elective III course for Semester VII Computer Engineering students taught by Prof. Yogita Patil in AY 2026-27. Total credits: 3 (Theory: 3 hours/week). Prerequisites: CE301 Machine Learning, CE305 Deep Learning, Probability and Linear Algebra.
title: CE413 Generative AI Course Specification

text: Module 1: Foundations of Deep Generative Models, Variational Autoencoders (VAEs), Latent Spaces and Reparameterization. Module 2: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), WGAN-GP, Conditional GANs, StyleGAN architectures. Module 3: Diffusion Models, DDPM, SDEs, Classifier-Free Guidance, Latent Diffusion and Stable Diffusion. Module 4: Autoregressive Transformers, GPT architectures, Attention mechanisms, FlashAttention, KV Caching. Module 5: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architectures, dense embeddings, FAISS indexing, hybrid BM25 search, Cross-Encoder reranking, RAGAS and hallucination evaluation. Module 6: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT, LoRA, QLoRA), RLHF, DPO, and AI Alignment.
title: CE413 Generative AI Course Specification

text: 1. Foster, D., Generative Deep Learning: Teaching Machines to Paint, Write, Compose, and Play, 2nd Edition, O'Reilly Media. 2. Goodfellow, I., Bengio, Y., Courville, A., Deep Learning, MIT Press. 3. Lewis, P. et al., Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks, NeurIPS.
title: CE413 Generative AI Course Specification

text: CE301 is a core course for Semester V Computer Engineering covering Supervised Learning (Linear Regression, Logistic Regression, SVMs, Decision Trees, Random Forests, Gradient Boosted Trees), Unsupervised Learning (K-Means, Hierarchical Clustering, PCA, t-SNE), Bias-Variance Tradeoff, and Cross-Validation strategies.
title: CE301 Machine Learning Course Specification

text: Laboratory assignments use Python, Scikit-learn, Pandas, and Matplotlib. Students implement gradient descent algorithms from scratch and benchmark ensemble models on Kaggle benchmark datasets.
title: CE301 Machine Learning Course Specification

text: CE402 covers Virtualization and Hypervisors, Containerization with Docker and Kubernetes, Cloud Service Models (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS), Cloud Storage and Consistency Models (CAP theorem, PACELC), Distributed Consensus (Raft, Paxos), Serverless computing with AWS Lambda, and Cloud Security.
title: CE402 Cloud Computing & Distributed Systems

title: Mandatory Disclosures, NBA and NAAC Accreditations

title: Research, Consultancy and Innovation Policy

title: Research, Consultancy and Innovation Policy

text:
Section 1: General Code of Student Conduct
All students admitted to Sardar Patel Institute of Technology must uphold the highest standards of academic
integrity, personal decorum, and mutual respect. Damaging campus property, unauthorized gatherings, identity
falsification, or substance abuse on the Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan campus will attract severe disciplinary action,
including suspension or permanent expulsion as determined by the Proctorial Committee.
title: Institutional Regulations: Code of Conduct and Anti-Ragging Policy
source_name: Student Code of Conduct & Anti-Ragging Policy

text:
Section 2: Anti-Ragging Statutory Guidelines
In strict compliance with UGC and AICTE regulations and the Maharashtra Prohibition of Ragging Act, ragging
in any form?physical abuse, mental harassment, verbal intimidation, or forced activity?is strictly prohibited both
inside and outside the college campus. Any student found guilty of ragging shall immediately be suspended,
and a First Information Report (FIR) will be lodged with the local Mumbai Police station. Anti-Ragging Squad
conducts unannounced vigils round the clock.
title: Institutional Regulations: Code of Conduct and Anti-Ragging Policy
source_name: Student Code of Conduct & Anti-Ragging Policy

text:
Section 1: Post-Result Verification and Photocopy Procedure
A candidate who desires to challenge the marks obtained in the End-Semester Examination (ESE) can apply for
verification of marks or procurement of a certified photocopy of the assessed answer book within seven working
days from the date of declaration of results on the institutional ERP portal. A fee of Rs. 300 per paper is levied
for verification.
title: Academic Regulations: Examination Grievance and Revaluation Rules

text:
Section 2: Revaluation and Expert Panel Review
Upon obtaining the photocopy, if discrepancies in assessment are identified, the student may apply for formal
revaluation within five days. The answer book is masked and forwarded to an external independent subject
expert. If the difference in marks exceeds 10% of the maximum marks, the revised score is awarded to the
student.
title: Academic Regulations: Examination Grievance and Revaluation Rules

title: Principal’s Message «  Sardar Patel Institute of Technology

text: I have great pleasure in expressing my thoughts as the Principal of Sardar Patel Institute of Technology (SPIT), the Numero Uno, self-financed, autonomous Institution of Maharashtra. We are a constituent of Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan, not just a conglomeration of more than 300 institutions, but a culture, a saga, a holy journey, started by Dr. K.M. Munshi with the support of Mahatma Gandhi in 1938. Imparting value-based education with Indian cultural ethos has always been the motto of Bhavan. Engineers & technologists form the backbone of any nation’s economic development. The world is presently undergoing very unprecedented, extraordinary, challenging time. A new normal is anticipated in many walks of life, including education. Such disruptions will come again and again in one or the other form. Engineers will work for 40-50 years of their life, they will have 3 to 4 diversified careers in technologies we are even unaware of.To make aspiring minds confident and future-proof, education must prepare them for a “marathon” rather than a “sprint”.SPIT makes continuous, sincere efforts towards this. We focus on “How to learn?” rather than “What to learn?”. We believe in multidisciplinary exposure to the learners, yet ensuring growth in one vertical, cherishing human sensitivity and empathy. We have thoughtfully articulated a unique academic model towards this. Our splendid academic performance, sparkling placements (quantitative and qualitative), enrollment for higher studies at the best places of the world, prizes won by our students in national/international level technical competitions, in past many years are the true testimonials for this. With the support of a dedicated and hardworking faculty and staff, the institute has achieved enviable visibility and ranking in a short span. On behalf of all stakeholders of SPIT, I welcome you to this family and look forward to your valuable association with us for a better tomorrow. Four years of engineering education at Sardar Patel Institute of Technology or two years post-graduation, will undoubtedly empower you to lead a successful life. Let’s grow together… Dr. Bhalchandra ChaudhariPrincipal, Sardar Patel Institute of Technology

title: Institutional Values «  Sardar Patel Institute of Technology

text: 1.Integrity– Integrity is defined as the quality of being honest and having strong moral principles. In an educational institution, where the sole aim of the organisation is to life the mindset of the students to soar new heights, integrity is of paramount importance. Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan’s Sardar Patel Institute of Technology takes pride in working with integrity and a sense of righteousness to hold itself to consistent moral and ethical standards. 2.Excellence– Excellence is the hallmark of consistency. Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan’s Sardar Patel Institute of Technology has consistently ranked among the top educational institutions in the city and state. It currently occupies a position in the 101 to 150 bracket of the National Institute Ranking Framework (NIRF). All this has been possible with dedicated input from the management and faculty members, who consistently try to mould the institution towards constant improvement and progress. 3.Social Sensitivity– The prime goal of an educational institution like Sardar Patel Institute of Technology, under the aegis of management like Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan, strives to make the society better in all respects by providing quality education. One of the highlights of the new curriculum under autonomy has been to provide relevant education that would make a difference to the society. The institution also tries to instill the values of social service among its students and faculty members by being a part of various social welfare schemes, and tie-ups with NGOs from time to time. 4.Globalization:Vasudev Kutumbakam– The whole universe is our family. With a strong belief in Vasudev Kutumbakam, Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan’s Sardar Patel Institute of Technology extends its services in education to one and all without any discrimination on any grounds whatsoever. It strives to consistently uplift the standard of education provided, with relevance to the current global trends and standards.

text: “Education would fail ignominiously in its objective if it manufactures only a robot and called him an economic man stressing the adjective economic and forgetting the substantive man. A university cannot afford to ignore the cultural aspects of education whatever studies it specilizes in. Science is a means, not an end. Whereas culture is an end in itself. Even though you may ultimately become a scientist, a doctor, or an engineer, you must while in college, absorb fundamental values which will make you a man of culture. An engineer has not merely to build bridges; he has to be a devoted husband, a kind father, a friendly neighbour, a dutiful citizen, and a man true to himself. He will have trials and tribulations; his heart will fail him at times; he will then need the strength which true culture alone can give.” Kulpati Dr. K. M. Munshi

title: Faculty Empowerment Policy «  Sardar Patel Institute of Technology

text: Faculty is the most important pillars of an institute. While students spend their 4 years in the institute, by large, teacher spends 30-40 years with the institute. Empowerment of faculty in turn is an empowerment of the student. While investment on empowerment of a student is recurring, the investment on empowerment of faculty gives long term returns. Institutes need to ensure continuous value addition of each and every faculty member. To encourage this, following schemes / policies are framed for various activities under the broad umbrella of faculty empowerment. Following policies/schemes are devised for empowerment faculty members.
title: Faculty Empowerment Policy «  Sardar Patel Institute of Technology

section: 1. Participation in Conference / Seminar/ Workshop / Exhibition /Technical Festivals /FDP / Training programs /STTP etc.
text: Empowerment comes through external exposure: Faculty members are encouraged to participate in thequality conferencesarranged by institutions of repute, centrally funded institutions, state govt. funded institutions, TEQIP funded institutions and other institutions in the country preferably in the bracket of 200 ranks in the NIRF. Faculty memberpublishing/presenting paperin the conference/workshop/ congress etc. will be reimbursed total expenditure towards this which include permissibletravel expenses, stay arrangement, permissible dearness allowance, and registration fees. Every faculty will be supportedonce in every yearfor such activity. Faculty members (who arenot authors) but interested in attending these prestigious conferences, workshops, seminars etc. will also be supported to the limit of75% of the actual expenses. The principal may accord sanction to additional conference/event for a particular faculty as a token of appreciation towardsvaluable contributionof an individual to the institute. Every faculty deputed for such external event, shallsubmit a report, and give a brief seminar in the department to the colleagues/students regarding the event/topic/paper.
title: Faculty Empowerment Policy «  Sardar Patel Institute of Technology

section: 2. Professional membership of Technical Societies such as IET, IEEE, IE(I), IETE, CSI, ACM, or any other professional society recommended by the respective HoD and Dean-Administration.
text: Empowerment comes through Collaboration: Every faculty will be encouraged to be the member of the professional societies in the domain. Institute will support 75% of the membership fees every year for every faculty with a maximum limit of Rs. 20000.
title: Faculty Empowerment Policy «  Sardar Patel Institute of Technology

text: Empowerment comes through Innovation: The IPR and Patents have become very important in today’s context for any higher education institute, in particular the technical education institution. Faculty need to be encouraged to innovate. Attempts be made to make them more innovative and creative. Projects, capstone project, mini project, give student opportunities to work together, work on new ideas. It may lead to start up / entrepreneurship. To encourage innovative works of the faculty, 100% financial support towards the expenses incurred in registering the new idea, patent will be provided by the institute. The application in this regard be forwarded through the Head of the Department. The institute level R&D committee under the Dean Academic & Research will evaluate this within a week. This committee will consist of 5 senior faculty across the institute covering broadly all domains of learning. The committee will scrutinize these proposals scrupulously. Based on the merits of the proposal a decision will be taken whether to extend the financial support or not. Financial support extended will be 100% of the total expenses (covering entire stages such as filing the patent, first examination, cross examination, response to the queries, all Govt fees and official charges of patent attorney, charges towards the certificate of award of the patent, etc). The patent will be property of the institute. It will be in the name of the institute. The faculty will be the authors for the patent. If the patent is rejected, the 50% expenses will be returned by the faculty to the institute. Only one patent per year per faculty will be supported.
title: Faculty Empowerment Policy «  Sardar Patel Institute of Technology

text: Empowerment comes from Industrial exploration: Faculty members are encouraged to visit industry, arrange industrial tours, do the industry internship to get real life flavors. Faculty will be financially supported for these activities. Every faculty will be supported once in every year for maximum 5 days. The permissible travelling and dearness allowances and permissible expenses towards stay will be reimbursed at actual. Faculty going for long duration industry internships will also be supported.
title: Faculty Empowerment Policy «  Sardar Patel Institute of Technology

text: Empowerment comes from quality learning material: Teacher is expected to refer good quality learning material. Teacher is expected to refer several world class books while preparing for the course to be taught. This is continuous process and demands the awareness of recent publications and literature. To facilitate every teacher is encouraged to procure the books. A financial support of actual amount spent on books limited toRs. 5000/- per yearwill be extended to every faculty member.
title: Faculty Empowerment Policy «  Sardar Patel Institute of Technology

section: 6. Assistance for enrollment for the MOOC’s courses.
text: Empowerment comes from accessibility: Open learning platform such as NPTEL, Coursera, edX offer great learning opportunity for today’s learners. This is enriching education. New courses on cutting edge technology, and of interdisciplinary nature can be studied on these platforms from the best universities of the world. The best teachers of these universities make such courses available to worldwide learners. Anytime, anywhere and offered at the individual pace are very distinctive and attractive features of these courses. Many reputed universities have started online specialization programs in emerging areas. IITs offer more than 400 courses on NPTEL/SWAYAM platform. Many of these courses are live courses and offered semester to semester. IITs also take Procter examinations and offer certificates to the learners who have successfully completed the registered course. All faculty members in the institute be encouraged to register for these courses and increase the bandwidth of the knowledge. To facilitate this, every faculty will be supported with100% of actual registration feesfor MOOC’s courses from NPTEL andupto 90 %for MOOCS from other platform. Teachers are expected to register for the courses related to new technology, inter disciplinary courses, advance mathematics and statistics related courses, and other value addition courses. Every teacher will be supported to register for one course per semester. Institute may also felicitate such Teachers who have registered and completed the MOOC’s course successfully in the Academic Council to appreciate the efforts of the teachers towards knowledge up gradation.
title: Faculty Empowerment Policy «  Sardar Patel Institute of Technology

section: 7. Tuition fees support to faculty for higher education/additional qualification.
text: Empowerment comes from higher education: Lifelong learning has become the essential attribute of today’s engineer. Disruption of technology is giving rise to several new fields. To sustain in such changing time, faculty members will have to continuously learn. To support faculty for enrolment to the higher education, tuition fees support will be extended to the faculty to the tune of50% of the actual fees paidfor the relevant programs at institute of high repute such as IITs/IIITs/NITs. Faulty requiring such support will make an application well in advance for such support. Presently such support will be extended for additional ME/M.Tech./MS Degree or Ph.D. program for regular and permanent faculty members.
title: Faculty Empowerment Policy «  Sardar Patel Institute of Technology

section: 8. Paper publication in the international conference outside the country.
text: Empowerment comes from international exploration: Faculty is encouraged to publish their quality work at the international conference of repute outside the country, present the paper, visit few universities nearby, and interact with domain experts. The support is extended towards registration fees, travel, stay and other expenses. For international event, such support will be limited toRs. 1,00,000/-. Faculty willing to publish a research paper at an international event outside the country should apply with the due recommendations of the HoD to Dean R&D. Institute level committee will scrutinize the application and will make recommendation to the principal. The faculty applying for this support, however, will make all possible attempts to fetch external support from various central and state funding agencies such as AICTE, SGBAU, UGC, DST, DoT, BARTI, SARTHI etc. If some external partial support is obtained, institute will give additional support limited toRs. 1,00,000/-. Every faculty deputed for such external event, shall submit a report and give a open talk in the institute inviting all faculty/students. Every faculty will be supported once in every 3 years for publishing paper at the international event outside the country.
title: Faculty Empowerment Policy «  Sardar Patel Institute of Technology

text: Empowerment comes from Support: Faculty/Department interested in the organization of such event will make a detailed proposal to the Dean R&D. The institute level committee will scrutinize the proposal and make its recommendations to the principal. If the amount requested is below Rs.1,00,000/-, Principal will accord the sanction to this proposal. Other proposals will be placed in the BoG meeting for sanction. However, the interested faculty should use this support as seed money and fetch external funding from various state and central funding agencies such as DST, AICTE, MU, UGC, and industries. One event per department per year will be supported by the institute. If there are more proposals, department will prioritize and recommend only one proposal in one semester.
title: Faculty Empowerment Policy «  Sardar Patel Institute of Technology

text: Empowerment comes from supporting seed money: The new entrant faculty will be supported by a seed money ofRs. 1,00,000/-for the research project to begin/to continue the journey of research. This will enable the young faculty to continue the research work of M.E/Ph.D after joining the institute. The faculty will write a research proposal. It will be scrutinized by the institute level R&D committee. The proposal will be recommended by the Dean R&D and approved by the principal. Every faculty is eligible for this support only once in his career, and within first 5 years of his/her service. Important Notes: Every faculty will be supported for any number of activities indicated in 1-7 with an annual limit ofRs. 50,000/- per faculty. Every faculty will be supported once in three years for the scheme no. 8. Scheme 9 and 10 are applicable to department and young faculty resp.
title: Faculty Empowerment Policy «  Sardar Patel Institute of Technology

text: Students are the most important pillars of the Institute. Holistic development of Students is the prime responsibility of the Institute. Their professional involvement in terms of participation in Conference, Competition, Hackathon, Sports, and Technology Training is extremely important. Financial support to students may increase their participation. Following Seven policies are devised for empowerment for students.
title: Students Empowerment Policy «  Sardar Patel Institute of Technology

section: 1. Participation in Conferences, Seminars, Workshops, Exhibitions, Technical Festivals, etc.
text: (Organized by Centrally funded institutions, State funded institution, TEQIP funded Institution and other institutions in 200 bracket of ranking by NIRF) Empowerment comes through Exposure Students are encouraged to take part in:Technical FestivalsandCompetitionssuch asTech-Fest, Mind-Spark, etc.National ConferencesSeminarsWorkshops Technical FestivalsandCompetitionssuch asTech-Fest, Mind-Spark, etc. National Conferences Seminars Workshops Students will greatly benefit from the numerous events and competitions that is offered to them. These experiences are necessary for an enriching engineering education. Any UG/PG/PhD student of the institute can avail such assistance once in a year and maximum twice in his/her program of study. Note:This assistance shall include registration fees, expenses towards food/stay/travelling, etc. limited toRs. 2000 per student per yearor actual expenditure incurred whatsoever is low. This assistance will beprovided only for those studentswho are partaking in the events in the form of presenting papers, projects, giving a technical talk, attending a technical quiz, participating in technical contests, etc. Studentsneed to apply in the prescribed formatalong with the necessary documents viz.participation certificate, receipts/tickets for the expensesfor this assistance after the event, duly recommended andsigned by the faculty coordinator/project guide/Supervisorfor the Dissertation/Research Guide to the HOD. The HOD needs to forward the application to the Dean SAER with the comments. The Dean SAER will study the documents and decide the amount to be reimbursed.
title: Students Empowerment Policy «  Sardar Patel Institute of Technology

section: 2. Professional membership of Technical Societies such as IET, IEEE, CSI, ACM etc.
text: Empowerment comes through Collaboration The Institute encourages maximum student participation in the activities of the professional societies in the technical field. The Institute understands the importance of such participation and will assist the students for membership. Membership in societies like IEEE & CSI allows students to be technically current, network with colleagues abroad and collaborate on research and projects with leading experts – all while taking advantage of specialized opportunities. Discover which society, or societies, best match your technical interests and take advantage of membership benefits ranging from access to cutting-edge technical magazines and conference discounts to educational resources and worldwide networking opportunities. Half the registration fees (limited to maximumRs. 1000/-) will be reimbursed by the institute. Note:The student needs to first pay the necessary fees and then apply for the reimbursement. Only one membership is permitted per year per student. Student with recommendation from the HOD will apply to the Dean SAER for the approval.
title: Students Empowerment Policy «  Sardar Patel Institute of Technology

section: 3. Assistance for registering Patents, Copyrights, IPRs.
text: Empowerment comes through Innovation Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) and Patents have become very important in today’s context for any higher education institute, in particular technical institutions. Innovation is often necessary for students to adapt and overcome the challenges of change. It fosters growth, learning and inner strength. Extensive projects give student opportunities to work on new ideas together. That is how startups are made. Note:An assistance of75% of the actual costinvolved in registering the new idea and patent will be provided by the Institute. The application in this regard be forwarded by the students through the Head of the Department and Dean SAER to the Dean R&D, which then will be evaluated by the Institute-level committee. The committee will consist of 5 members across the institute covering broadly all domains of learning. The committee will meet once every month and scrutinize these proposals scrupulously. Based on the merits of the proposal a decision will be taken whether to extend the financial support or not. Patent shall be in the name of the institute. The student/students will be the Authors.
title: Students Empowerment Policy «  Sardar Patel Institute of Technology

section: 4. Participation in external Technical Training Programs.
text: Empowerment comes from Preparation To be a successful engineer in the current atmosphere of rapid technological advancement, one must constantly learn and prepare themselves. The Industry requires skilled engineers to be part of the said advancement. Centrally Funded Institutions like IITs and the Tech Industry regularly arrange valuable training programs for students who are willing. Students should exploit such training programs offered to them to increase their knowledge base and be employable in a highly competitive and ever-changing market space. Note:A financial support limited to50% of the registration fees or Rs. 5000/-whatsoever is lower will be extended to every student once during the program of study. Besides this 50% expenses towards travel and food/stay orRs. 500/- per daywhatsoever is lower, limited to maximumRs. 2500will also be extended.
title: Students Empowerment Policy «  Sardar Patel Institute of Technology

section: 5. Assistance for enrollment for the MOOC courses.
text: Empowerment comes from accessibility The Internet has paved the way for open learning platforms such as NPTEL, Coursera, edX, which offer great learning opportunities for today’s learners. Students can learn from content beyond the syllabus, courses beyond structure, interdisciplinary courses from the best universities of the world, at their own pace. Many institutions and Universities have started to formally accept the credits earned by students from open learning platform. IITs offer more than 400 courses on their NPTEL/SWAYAM platform. All students in the institute must register for these online courses and increase the bandwidth of the learning. Note:Students will be supported to the tune of75% of actual registration fees or maximum Rs. 2,000/-whichever is less for NPTEL / edX / Coursera / Audacity courses per year. This support shall be extended to maximum one course per semester per student.
title: Students Empowerment Policy «  Sardar Patel Institute of Technology

text: Empowerment comes from Exploration The Institute strives hard for possible interactions with industries on all fronts. AICTE strongly advocates the need of Industry Internships, Industry Visits, Internships, and Industry sponsored real-life projects, to enrich the learning experience. Students must explore various domains and get hands-on experience to get an edge over others. Note:Departments are expected to arrange at least one industrial visit per year. Similarly, a focused technical tour for the post graduate students will be arranged by every department every year. For Industrial visits, financial support ofRs. 500/- per day per studentwill be extended for outstation industrial visits. For long term industrial tours (more than 3 days), a support ofRs. 2000/-will be extended for every student once in every year towards the expenses incurred. (Travel, Food, Hotel etc.).
title: Students Empowerment Policy «  Sardar Patel Institute of Technology

section: 7. Assistance for Research-Flavored Projects and Dissertations
text: Empowerment comes from Performance Research Projects, Dissertations give opportunity for students to innovate, design, fabricate, experiment on different ideas. The Field of Research is ever-growing, where great academic institutions and companies are extensively funding useful research. Students need to be encouraged to work on industry relevant hardware projects than limiting themselves on simulations. Note:Interested students will write a brief proposal giving the background, problem statement, budget, and phases of the execution to the department. Such proposals will be scrutinized thoroughly and recommended for support accordingly. The Institute-level Committee under Dean R&D will take the decision for extending such support. A financial assistance of70% of actual cost incurredshall be reimbursed. There will be no ceiling for this support. This support shall be extended to every PG dissertation or UG project (minimum group of 3 students). There will be Institute-level Annual Exhibitions, demonstrating these supported projects, and an award in the form of certificate and medal will be given to the Best Project/Dissertation of the year. IMPORTANT NOTE:Every regular student can take benefit of one or any number of empowerment schemes provided that total support in one financial year does not exceedRs. 6000/- per student. This ceiling excludes item no. 6 & 7.

text: We have moved beyond conventional classrooms. We have introduced four “Studio Mode” core courses. This means that in core subjects, students don’t just sit in lectures. They build, prototype, code, and present – just like in a design studio or a startup. Learning by doing.

text: Along with technical depth, we give breadth. A student can do a Minor in Management from SPJIMR or a Minor in Banking Technologies with Barclays – learn fintech, risk, digital banking directly from industry leaders. Alternatively, one can do a Minor in Computer or AIML while majoring in Electronics and Telecommunication. There are several other minors to match every career path. We even offer a Minor in specializations such as Mathematics / Physics / Systems Engineering. Plus: A Research Internship in 7th semester or an Industry Internship in 8th semester. Every year around 50 of our students do a research internship at IITs/BARC/TIFR, and the remaining pursue the industry internship. Students opting for the research internship continue their work in the eighth semester in the form of a project. So, by the time you graduate, you already have 1 year of real research experience at elite institutions.

text: Our students are in Google, Microsoft, Intel, AMD, Facebook, Uber, JPMC, Barclays, Nvidia and several other deep tech companies. Program Overview The Bachelor of Technology (B.Tech) in Computer Science and Engineering (CSE) at Sardar Patel
Institute of Technology (SPIT) is a comprehensive four-year undergraduate program designed to
equip students with a solid foundation in computer science principles, engineering methodologies,
and practical applications. The program emphasizes both theoretical knowledge and hands-on
experience to prepare graduates for the rapidly evolving field of technology. Students are exposed to a curriculum that covers core areas such as mathematics, programming,
data structures, algorithms, computer networks, Computer Architecture and Organization ,
operating systems, etc, while also delving into advanced topics like artificial intelligence, neural
network , soft computing, machine learning, data analytics, NLP, Image Processing, Signal Processing
,Computer Vision, Explainable AI, Human Machine Interaction, cloud computing, Blockchain,
Quantum computing and cyber security. Through a combination of classroom learning, laboratory
work, and real-world projects, the program ensures that students are not only proficient in technical
skills but also adept at problem-solving and critical thinking. SPIT's B.Tech CSE program is designed to meet industry standards, with regular updates to the
curriculum to reflect the latest technological advancements. Graduates are well-prepared to pursue
careers in diverse fields such as software development, Machine Learning, Data Visualization, Data
science, User Experience Design, Data Analysis, network security, Cloud computing, Backend and
Front end development and more, or to continue their education with advanced degrees. Through high-quality academic programs enriched with today's National Education Policy(NEP-2020)
that offer a unique blend of teaching, research, activity-based learning including Seva Satva, minors
etc. that strengthens learner’s ability to solve problems, expand knowledge base, work
independently, think critically, and find new ways to apply Science and Engineering concepts to
benefit society. In addition to technical training, the program also focuses on the development of soft skills,
teamwork, and leadership qualities, ensuring that students are well-rounded professionals ready to
contribute to the global tech industry. Students work alongside faculty members who are leaders in their respective disciplines, have access
to labs equipped with the latest technologies, and are connected to a comprehensive University
providing breadth and depth of opportunities. As a result, our students acquire critical thinking
capabilities as well as practically oriented skills that are prized by prestigious companies and
academic institutions of National and International Importance. All faculty members of the Department of Computer Science and Engineering are strongly
committed to supporting your success. In return, we know you will study hard, seek out and respect
the opinions of faculties and find opportunities to give back to your society. The efforts are
consciously planned for the overall development of students. This leads our students to become
competent, innovative, socially-responsible and dynamic. We are confident that our students will
emerge as assets not only to this institution but also to the entire society, and the nation at large.

text: SPIT actively encourages students to engage in research internships as a means of developing analytical thinking, problem-solving skills, and academic curiosity. These internships allow students to work on research-oriented problems under faculty guidance or at external institutions and laboratories, helping prepare them for higher studies, research careers, and innovation-driven roles. text: SPIT has a formal deferred placement policy that allows students to delay immediate campus recruitment after graduation. This flexibility enables students to pursue entrepreneurship, freelancing, research, or focused skill-building for a defined period, while retaining the opportunity to return to campus placements in subsequent cycles if required. Supporting Documents / Links: Placement Policy Placement Summary

title: IT Infrastructure «  Sardar Patel Institute of Technology

text: Introduction In the era of digital revolution, advanced IT Infrastructure is a need of time for every academic institution. In view of this, institute has provided state of the art and well maintained IT Infrastructure to students and faculty members. This includes high-speed servers with large storage & processing power. Following is a brief description about the services that have been hosted on the servers. Wi-Fi The entire campus has been Wi-Fi enabled to provide mobility to the users in accessing various services available on institute’s network. This Wi-Fi network allows faculty, staff and students to log on to the Internet at any point of time. This wireless layer is placed on top of highly dense network with high level of security using username password based authentication. Storage S.P.I.T. has setup ownCloud, a file and document sharing utility similar to the popular Dropbox, for use by the S.P.I.T. staff. The utility supports storing and sharing of files, documents, contacts, calendar, tasks etc. It also supports version control and syncing with Windows/Linux/Mac desktops and Android and iOS based devices. NTP Server S.P.I.T has setup it’s own internal NTP server to keep it’s network devices & servers with the standard date & time. This timeserver also gets synchronized with external regional timeservers with time drift less than a few milliseconds. Moodle S.P.I.T. has hosted Moodle, public domain course management software, for use by faculty and students for the courses running in the current semester. All students and faculty members are periodically enrolled in various courses. Apart from online dissemination of course material, Moodle supports a host of other features for every course like news, blogs, discussion forums and facility for online submission of assignments and quizzes. Moodle at S.P.I.T. can be accessed athttps://moodle.spit.ac.in DNS S.P.I.T. has it’s own DNS server for name resolution of it’s website & subdomains. All nodes connected within S.P.I.T. network use the DNS server for faster Internet browsing by caching the name resolution results of frequently visited websites. DSPACE Server (Digital Repository) All-important documents are available and hosted in digital format on a server named as DSPACE. This is a digital repository of all documents. This server runs on open source software. The documents can be searched easily using a keyword. The documents and data segregation, department wise, community wise, etc. is supported. This facilitates centralized data storage accessible from institution intranet. The facility is available athttp://dspace.spit.ac.in:8081/jspui/within S.P.I.T. Website Apropos to mandatory requirements of AICTE, college has informative website:https://www.spit.ac.in. The information on website is regularly updated. Students, faculty members and all stakeholders access website regularly. Apart from statutory information, website also hosts useful academic resources for students, such as exam papers, scheme and syllabus, NPTEL Videos, academic schedule, exam schedule, etc. Mail Server and Client The E-mail facility is managed through G Suite, which provides us web, based email client, and built in chat facility, Google Docs, Google Apps, Google Sites and few other facilities as well. Every faculty & student has an e-mail ID onspit.ac.indomain. Internet The Institute’s network is linked to the Internet via a set of dedicated leased lines enabling round-the-clock Internet connectivity on the campus. The Internet leased lines are availed from different service providers so that the provision of redundant ISPs is there in order to have seamless connectivity across the campus. All the Internet Service Providers (ISPs) from whom the Institute has procured Internet bandwidth have installed fibre optics link from the campus to their hub. This ensures very high quality of bandwidth to the Internet. The Institute has 1 GBPS bandwidth to the Internet. It is technologically equipped to increase it up to 2 GBPS as and when the need for more bandwidth arises. There is a dedicated Internet browsing centre within the library for students. This Internet browsing centre is open to students during all working hours and even beyond office hours in order to have access to information available on Internet as when required.
